question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To cut no ice

options.text: To have no influence or effect

explanation: Cut no ice = कोई असर न डालना। Example: His excuses cut no ice with the teacher.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To grasp the nettle

options.text: To tackle a difficult situation boldly

explanation: Grasp the nettle = कठिन समस्या का डटकर सामना करना। Example: It is time to grasp the nettle and fix the budget.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A chip on one's shoulder

options.text: A lasting feeling of resentment or grievance

explanation: A chip on one's shoulder = मन में दबी शिकायत या कुंठा। Example: He has a chip on his shoulder about not studying at a big college.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A Pyrrhic victory

options.text: A victory won at too great a cost

explanation: Pyrrhic victory = ऐसी जीत जिसकी भारी क़ीमत चुकानी पड़े। Example: Winning the case but losing all his savings was a Pyrrhic victory.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To burn one's boats

options.text: To cut off every chance of retreat

explanation: Burn one's boats = वापसी के सारे रास्ते बंद कर लेना। Example: By quitting his job without another offer, he burnt his boats.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Cloud-cuckoo-land
explanation: Cloud-cuckoo-land = ख़्याली पुलाव की दुनिया। Example: Planning to double sales without a team is living in cloud-cuckoo-land.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: At sixes and sevens

options.text: In a state of confusion or disorder

explanation: At sixes and sevens = अस्त-व्यस्त, उलझन में। Example: The office was at sixes and sevens after the shifting.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pour oil on troubled waters

options.text: To calm a quarrel or a tense situation

explanation: Pour oil on troubled waters = झगड़े को शांत करना। Example: The principal poured oil on troubled waters between the two groups.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: In the doldrums

options.text: In the middle of a heavy storm
In a state of low spirits or inactivity
In a state of great joy

explanation: In the doldrums = उदासी या ठहराव की दशा में। Example: The tourism trade has been in the doldrums this year.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To throw down the gauntlet
explanation: Throw down the gauntlet = चुनौती देना। Example: The opposition threw down the gauntlet to the government.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take the wind out of someone's sails

options.text: To make a boat move faster
To suddenly reduce someone's confidence or excitement

explanation: Take the wind out of someone's sails = किसी का जोश ठंडा कर देना। Example: The harsh review took the wind out of the director's sails.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To lead someone up the garden path

options.text: To walk with someone in the evening
To show someone a beautiful garden

explanation: Lead someone up the garden path = झाँसा देना, बहकाना। Example: The agent led us up the garden path with false promises.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To sail close to the wind

options.text: To take a risk by nearly breaking the rules

explanation: Sail close to the wind = नियमों की सीमा पर जोखिम भरा काम करना। Example: The trader sailed close to the wind with his tax returns.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To toe the line

options.text: To stand in a long queue
To obey the rules or follow orders

explanation: Toe the line = नियमों या आदेशों का पालन करना। Example: Every new recruit must toe the line.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To grease someone's palm
explanation: Grease someone's palm = रिश्वत देना। Example: He greased the clerk's palm to get the file moved.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To cast pearls before swine

options.text: To offer something valuable to those who cannot appreciate it
To donate generously to the poor
To sell jewels at a high price

explanation: Cast pearls before swine = अयोग्य को अनमोल चीज़ देना (भैंस के आगे बीन बजाना)। Example: Teaching poetry to the bored students was casting pearls before swine.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To rest on one's laurels

options.text: To be content with past success and make no further effort

explanation: Rest on one's laurels = पिछली सफलता पर ही संतुष्ट होकर बैठ जाना। Example: The champion rested on his laurels and lost the title.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To keep the wolf from the door

options.text: To guard the house at night

explanation: Keep the wolf from the door = भुखमरी या ग़रीबी से बचे रहना। Example: His small pension just keeps the wolf from the door.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To read the riot act

options.text: To scold or warn someone severely
To read a law aloud in public

explanation: Read the riot act = कड़ी फटकार लगाना। Example: The coach read the riot act to the careless players.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A bee in one's bonnet
explanation: A bee in one's bonnet = किसी बात की सनक सवार होना। Example: He has a bee in his bonnet about early morning walks.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To feather one's nest

options.text: To enrich oneself, often by misusing one's position
To give gifts to one's family
To build a house for birds

explanation: Feather one's nest = पद का लाभ उठाकर अपनी जेब भरना। Example: The officer feathered his nest with public money.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take French leave

options.text: To go abroad for higher studies

explanation: Take French leave = बिना अनुमति ग़ैरहाज़िर होना। Example: He took French leave and went to watch the match.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To show the white feather
explanation: Show the white feather = कायरता दिखाना। Example: The soldier refused to show the white feather.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To stew in one's own juice

options.text: To suffer the results of one's own actions

explanation: Stew in one's own juice = अपने किए का फल भुगतना। Example: Let him stew in his own juice for a while.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A cat's paw

options.text: A person who is used by another to do an unpleasant or risky job

explanation: A cat's paw = दूसरे के हाथ की कठपुतली। Example: The clerk was only a cat's paw of the corrupt manager.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To carry coals to Newcastle

options.text: To do a very heavy job
To do something unnecessary or useless

explanation: Carry coals to Newcastle = जहाँ चीज़ भरपूर हो वहीं और ले जाना (व्यर्थ का काम)। Example: Gifting rice to a farmer is like carrying coals to Newcastle.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To hang fire

options.text: To delay or hesitate in taking action

explanation: Hang fire = देर करना, टालमटोल करना। Example: The road project is hanging fire for want of funds.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To steal a march on someone

options.text: To gain an advantage by acting before others
To rob someone on the road

explanation: Steal a march on someone = पहले चाल चलकर बढ़त ले लेना। Example: The rival firm stole a march on us by launching earlier.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To come a cropper

options.text: To fail badly or fall heavily

explanation: Come a cropper = बुरी तरह गिरना या असफल होना। Example: He came a cropper in the final exam.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Hobson's choice

options.text: A choice with no real alternative

explanation: Hobson's choice = ऐसा चुनाव जिसमें विकल्प ही न हो (लो या छोड़ो)। Example: With only one bus left, it was Hobson's choice.
